caption: The drawing depicts a single wooden chair with an ornate design, positioned angled to the right on a plain, light beige background. The chair’s frame and legs are dark, rendered in shades of deep brown and black, with turned and carved details present in the legs, stretchers, and backrest posts. The backrest is tall, with two vertical, carved side supports featuring multiple rounded knobs and a central splat composed of three straight vertical rods flanked by two curling, scroll-shaped designs on either side. Across the top and bottom of the backrest, there are horizontal rails decorated with further scrollwork patterns. The seat of the chair is lighter in color, possibly representing cane or woven wicker, and distinctly contrasts with the darker wooden frame. The bottom of the chair includes two more stretchers, with the front stretcher showcasing an openwork scroll motif similar to the backrest, and all legs are slightly splayed out at the feet. The artist’s name, “Arthur Johnson,” is inscribed in small letters in the lower right corner.
title: High-Back Side Chair
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
